## Make your mark

Create a simple personal mark from **your initials, a landscape idea, or both**. Your starting image may be hand drawn or created with an approved AI image tool. The finished logo must be your own simplified design.

[Open the printable Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1twC4psThGx-QTd_yiHPICXmogqdAH5zv1JRjKyQnUIM/edit){.btn .btn-primary}
[Download the printable PDF](../../assets/name-tag-photopea/personal-logo-worksheet.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

![Four-step example showing a landscape inspiration becoming a simple coloured vector logo](../../assets/name-tag-photopea/landscape-to-logo.svg){fig-alt="A hand-drawn or AI-made landscape reference is reduced to a sun, mountain, and river, rebuilt with simple shapes in Photopea, and finished as an original coloured logo."}

## 1. Start with an idea

Use either:

- your own quick drawing; or
- an approved AI-made image created from your own prompt.

Do **not** trace every detail. Circle only **two or three useful ingredients**, such as a mountain triangle, a sun circle, a river curve, or your initials.

## 2. Sketch three different ideas

Use the worksheet. Draw three simple marks quickly.

1. **Initials only**
2. **Landscape shapes only**
3. **Initials + one landscape shape**

Choose the idea with the clearest silhouette, not the most detail.

## 3. Know the file types

<figure>
  <img src="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6b/Bitmap_VS_SVG.svg" alt="A raster image becomes blocky when enlarged while an SVG vector stays smooth" style="display:block;max-width:720px;width:100%;margin-inline:auto">
  <figcaption><strong>Raster:</strong> pixels, such as JPG and PNG. <strong>Vector:</strong> paths, such as SVG. Image: <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bitmap_VS_SVG.svg">Yug, Wikimedia Commons</a>, CC BY-SA 2.5.</figcaption>
</figure>

For this logo, keep the editable Photopea file and export an **SVG** master. A PNG copy is useful later for engraving.

## 4. Rebuild your selected sketch in Photopea

Follow these steps after you have circled the sketch you want to develop.

1. Open [Photopea](https://www.photopea.com/) and choose **File > New**.
2. Set **Width: 1000 px**, **Height: 1000 px**, and **Background: Transparent**. Select **Create**.
3. Choose **File > Open & Place** and select a clear photo or scan of your sketch.
4. In the **Layers** panel, double-click the new layer name and rename it `REFERENCE`.
5. Set the `REFERENCE` layer **Opacity to 30%**. Select the lock icon so you cannot move it by accident.
6. Select the **New Layer** icon. Name the new layer for the part you will draw, such as `SUN`, `MOUNTAIN`, or `INITIALS`.
7. Press **U** for a Shape tool. In the top bar, choose a shape, set **Fill to black**, and set **Stroke to none**. Drag to draw circles, rectangles, or polygons.
8. Press **P** for the Pen tool when you need a custom shape. Click to make straight corners. Click and drag only when you need a curve. Close the path by clicking the first point.
9. Press **T** for the Type tool if your mark uses initials. Choose a bold, readable sans-serif font. Keep the text layer editable while you test the idea.
10. Press **V** for the Move tool. Select a layer, then use **Ctrl+T** to resize, rotate, or move that part. Hold **Shift** while resizing to keep its proportions.
11. Keep one idea on one layer or in one clearly named group. Duplicate a layer before changing it so you can compare versions.
12. Hide the `REFERENCE` layer by selecting its eye icon. Your logo should still look clear as one black silhouette.

Use pixels here because this is a scale-free logo master, not the final physical name tag. You will use inches when you place the logo on the 11 by 4 inch name-tag canvas.

### If you start with type

1. Keep one editable text layer.
2. Duplicate it.
3. Right-click the copy and choose **Convert to Shape**.
4. Move, overlap, rotate, or combine the shapes.

Do not convert your only editable text layer. Keep the original hidden in the PSD so spelling and font choices can still be changed.

### If you start with a drawing

1. Photograph it straight on in bright, even light.
2. Crop and increase the contrast.
3. Choose **Image > Vectorize Bitmap**.
4. Use very few colours.
5. Remove bumps, tiny pieces, and unwanted holes.

## 5. Add simple colour

Use **two or three colours at most**. Choose one main colour, one supporting colour, and an optional accent.

- Keep strong light-dark contrast.
- Do not use colour to hide an unclear shape.
- Keep a black version for engraving.
- Avoid gradients and tiny coloured details for the first version.

Colour can add mood: warm colours may feel energetic, while blues and greens may feel calm or connected to land and water. These are choices, not fixed rules.

## 6. Run four quick tests

- **Small:** is it recognizable at about 25 mm wide?
- **Black:** does the silhouette still work?
- **White:** does it work on a dark background?
- **Grayscale:** does the idea survive without colour?

If a thin line disappears, thicken it. If a small gap closes, open it. If the mark needs colour to make sense, simplify it.

## 7. Save the logo system

Save:

- editable `lastname-logo-master.psd`
- `lastname-logo-colour.svg`
- `lastname-logo-dark.svg`
- `lastname-logo-light.svg`
- `lastname-logo-gray.svg`
- transparent `lastname-logo.png`

Choose **File > Export As > SVG** for the vector master. Keep the PSD so you can revise it.

Before submitting, reopen the exported SVG in Photopea. Confirm that it has the correct shapes, no missing letters, no accidental background, and no pieces outside the canvas.

::: {.callout-tip title="Ready for the name tag?"}
Bring the transparent PNG and the editable PSD to the [Name + Logo engraving worksheet](../03-laser-cutting/01-name-logo.qmd). You will test the proportions on paper before building the final file.
:::
